cases.surface_condition: right_first is a common noun 'language'/'languages' when left_last is an adjectival/adverbial cluster (e.g. most/commonly/spoken)
cases.blamed_rule: Cuts that separate two independently meaningful lexical clusters (e.g., noun phrase + independent verb phrase) where both clusters contain content words (nouns, verbs, numerals) and do not leave a dangling single function word are likely to score higher. (Prediction to test: cuts after a main verb or after a multi-word noun phrase with a numeral/name often score high.)
cases.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: Downgrade markers whose right-side begins with 'language' or 'languages' when the left-side ends with a short adjectival/adverbial cluster (left_last in {most, commonly, spoken, more, less}) — target band 0–50.

cases.surface_condition: marker splits a numeric+unit phrase: left_last is NUM and right_first is a multiplier/unit word (e.g. million, billion, percent, thousand)
cases.blamed_rule: Is the token immediately before the marker a numeral/date/percentage/name? If yes, bias score upward.
cases.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: Do NOT apply the generic numerator boost when the marker splits a numeric + unit/scale token sequence. If left_last is NUM and right_first is in {million, billion, thousand, percent, % ,k,m,mi,kg,miles,signatures} then move marker into a lower target band 0–40.

cases.surface_condition: left_last is a short organization/name token (e.g. parenthood, university, inc) and right_first is a subordinating token like 'due'/'because'/'to' that continues the clause
cases.blamed_rule: Left or right stretch that ends or begins with a lexical token translators typically render reliably will tend to raise the measured value.
cases.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: Reduce boost for cuts that end immediately after organization/name tokens when the right-first token is a subordinating word. If left_last is in {foundation, association, parenthood, university, corporation, company, inc, ltd, group, authority, service} AND right_first in {due, because, to, on, that, which, who, of} then move marker to target band 0–45.

summary: The prompt systematically over-boosts cuts adjacent to surface tokens that look lexical (numbers, short names, adjective clusters) even when those cuts split multi-token constructs (numeric+unit, adjectival cluster before a head noun) or leave a fragment that the remainder will resolve/contradict. Add targeted downgrades: (1) block numeric boosts that split number+unit phrases, (2) avoid treating adjectival clusters before the noun 'language' as independently high, and (3) reduce name/organization boosts when the right side begins a subordinating continuation (due/because/to). These rules keep the existing high-score heuristics but prevent the common over-trust mistakes.
